title: Dilmun Civilization Flourishes
description: The ancient Dilmun trading civilization thrived on Bahrain, serving as a key hub linking Mesopotamia and the Indus Valley.

title: Bahrain Embraces Islam
description: Bahrain was among the first regions to adopt Islam during the lifetime of the Prophet Muhammad.

title: Portuguese Conquest
description: The Portuguese Empire seized Bahrain, controlling the islands and their lucrative pearl trade for about eight decades.

title: Al Khalifa Dynasty Established
description: The Al Khalifa family captured Bahrain from Persian rule, founding the dynasty that still rules the country today.

title: First Gulf Oil Discovery
description: Bahrain became the first country on the Arabian side of the Gulf to discover oil, transforming its economy.

title: Independence from Britain
description: Bahrain declared full independence, ending its status as a British protectorate.

title: Kingdom of Bahrain Proclaimed
description: Bahrain adopted a new constitution and became a constitutional monarchy as the ruler took the title of King.

title: Cyrus the Great Founds Persian Empire
description: Cyrus the Great established the Achaemenid Empire, which became the largest empire of the ancient world.

title: Conquest of Babylon
description: Cyrus captured Babylon and issued the Cyrus Cylinder, often regarded as an early charter of human rights.

title: Fall of the Achaemenids to Alexander
description: Alexander the Great defeated Darius III and burned Persepolis, ending the Achaemenid Empire.

title: Sasanian Empire Established
description: Ardashir I founded the Sasanian Empire, the last Persian empire before the rise of Islam.

title: Arab Conquest of Persia
description: Muslim Arab armies defeated the Sasanians, leading to the gradual Islamization of Persia.

title: Safavid Dynasty Founded
description: Shah Ismail I established the Safavid dynasty and made Twelver Shia Islam the state religion of Persia.

title: Persia Renamed Iran
description: Reza Shah Pahlavi formally requested that the country be known internationally as Iran.

title: Islamic Revolution
description: The monarchy was overthrown and Ayatollah Khomeini established the Islamic Republic of Iran.

title: Sumerian Cities of Mesopotamia
description: The Sumerians built the world's first cities such as Uruk in Mesopotamia, the cradle of civilization.

title: Invention of Cuneiform Writing
description: Sumerians developed cuneiform, one of the earliest known writing systems in human history.

title: Code of Hammurabi
description: Babylonian King Hammurabi issued one of the earliest and most complete written legal codes.

title: Neo-Babylonian Golden Age
description: Under Nebuchadnezzar II, Babylon flourished and is associated with the legendary Hanging Gardens.

title: Founding of Baghdad
description: The Abbasid Caliph al-Mansur founded Baghdad, which became a leading center of learning in the Islamic Golden Age.

title: Mongol Sack of Baghdad
description: Mongol forces destroyed Baghdad and ended the Abbasid Caliphate, devastating its libraries and population.

title: Kingdom of Iraq Independence
description: Iraq gained independence from British mandate rule and joined the League of Nations.

title: US-Led Invasion Topples Saddam
description: A US-led coalition invaded Iraq and overthrew the regime of Saddam Hussein.

title: Kingdom of Israel Under David
description: According to biblical tradition, King David united the tribes of Israel and made Jerusalem his capital.

title: Solomon's Temple in Jerusalem
description: King Solomon is traditionally credited with building the First Temple in Jerusalem.

title: Destruction of the First Temple
description: The Babylonians destroyed Jerusalem and its Temple, beginning the Babylonian exile of the Jews.

title: Roman Destruction of the Second Temple
description: Roman forces under Titus destroyed the Second Temple in Jerusalem during the Jewish revolt.

title: Declaration of the State of Israel
description: David Ben-Gurion proclaimed the establishment of the modern State of Israel.

title: Six-Day War
description: Israel fought neighboring Arab states and captured the West Bank, Gaza, Sinai, and the Golan Heights.

title: Peace Treaty with Egypt
description: Israel and Egypt signed a landmark peace treaty following the Camp David Accords.

title: Nabataeans Establish Petra
description: The Nabataean kingdom made Petra its capital, a thriving caravan city carved into rose-colored rock.

title: Roman Annexation of Nabataea
description: Rome annexed the Nabataean kingdom, incorporating the region into the province of Arabia Petraea.

title: Battle of Yarmouk
description: Muslim armies decisively defeated the Byzantines near the Yarmouk River in present-day Jordan.

title: Emirate of Transjordan Created
description: The British established the Emirate of Transjordan under Emir Abdullah following World War I.

title: Independence of Jordan
description: Transjordan gained independence from Britain and became a sovereign kingdom under King Abdullah I.

title: Peace Treaty with Israel
description: Jordan signed a peace treaty with Israel, becoming the second Arab state to normalize relations.

title: Petra Named a Wonder of the World
description: Petra was selected as one of the New Seven Wonders of the World, boosting Jordanian tourism.

title: Founding of Kuwait City
description: Kuwait City was established as a settlement that grew into a major trading and pearling port.

title: Al Sabah Dynasty Begins
description: The Al Sabah family was chosen to lead Kuwait, founding the ruling dynasty that continues today.

title: Anglo-Kuwaiti Agreement
description: Kuwait signed a protective agreement with Britain to safeguard against Ottoman influence.

title: Discovery of Major Oil Fields
description: The vast Burgan oil field was discovered, eventually making Kuwait one of the world's leading oil exporters.

title: Independence from Britain
description: Kuwait gained full independence, ending the protectorate relationship with the United Kingdom.

title: Iraqi Invasion of Kuwait
description: Iraq invaded and annexed Kuwait, triggering the Gulf War and an international coalition response.

title: Liberation of Kuwait
description: A US-led coalition expelled Iraqi forces, restoring Kuwait's sovereignty after months of occupation.

title: Phoenician Maritime Civilization
description: Phoenician city-states like Tyre and Sidon became dominant Mediterranean traders and seafarers.

title: Spread of the Phoenician Alphabet
description: Phoenicians developed an alphabet that became the basis for Greek, Latin, and many modern scripts.

title: Roman Province of Phoenicia
description: Pompey incorporated the region into the Roman Empire, and Berytus became a famed center of law.

title: Ottoman Rule Begins
description: The Ottoman Empire took control of Mount Lebanon, ruling the region for four centuries.

title: Independence of Lebanon
description: Lebanon gained full independence from French mandate rule and adopted its National Pact.

title: Lebanese Civil War Begins
description: A devastating civil war erupted along sectarian lines, lasting fifteen years.

title: End of the Civil War
description: The Taif Agreement brought an end to the Lebanese Civil War and reformed the political system.

title: Magan Copper Trade
description: Ancient Oman, known as Magan, was a key source of copper traded across Mesopotamia and the Indus.

title: Oman Adopts Islam
description: Oman peacefully embraced Islam during the lifetime of the Prophet Muhammad.

title: Portuguese Capture of Muscat
description: Portuguese forces seized the coastal city of Muscat, controlling it for over a century.

title: Expulsion of the Portuguese
description: The Ya'rubid dynasty drove the Portuguese out of Muscat, restoring Omani control of the coast.

title: Al Said Dynasty Founded
description: Ahmad bin Said established the Al Said dynasty, which still rules Oman today.

title: Sultan Qaboos Begins Modernization
description: Sultan Qaboos came to power and launched sweeping modernization of Oman's economy and infrastructure.

title: Oman Joins the United Nations
description: Oman became a member of the United Nations, marking its emergence as a recognized modern state.

title: Philistines Settle the Coast
description: The Philistines established a confederation of city-states along the southern coast of Canaan.

title: Muslim Conquest of Jerusalem
description: Caliph Umar took control of Jerusalem, beginning centuries of Islamic rule over the region.

title: Dome of the Rock Completed
description: The Umayyads completed the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem, an iconic masterpiece of Islamic architecture.

title: Crusaders Capture Jerusalem
description: European Crusaders seized Jerusalem and established the Crusader Kingdom of Jerusalem.

title: British Mandate Era Begins
description: Following World War I, Britain took control of Palestine, governing it under a League of Nations mandate.

title: Declaration of Independence
description: The Palestine Liberation Organization proclaimed the State of Palestine in Algiers.

title: UN Non-Member Observer State
description: The UN General Assembly granted Palestine non-member observer state status.

title: Al Thani Family Settles Qatar
description: The Al Thani family migrated to the Qatari peninsula and became its leading dynasty.

title: Anglo-Qatari Treaty
description: A treaty with Britain recognized Qatar as a distinct entity separate from Bahrain.

title: Discovery of Oil
description: Oil was discovered in Qatar at Dukhan, eventually transforming the nation's economy.

title: Independence from Britain
description: Qatar declared full independence, ending its status as a British protectorate.

title: Launch of Al Jazeera
description: Qatar launched the Al Jazeera satellite network, which became one of the most influential media outlets in the Arab world.

title: North Field Gas Development
description: Qatar began large-scale liquefied natural gas exports, becoming a global LNG leader.

title: Qatar Hosts the FIFA World Cup
description: Qatar became the first Arab nation to host the FIFA World Cup.

title: Birth of the Prophet Muhammad
description: The Prophet Muhammad, founder of Islam, was born in Mecca around this year.

title: The Hijra to Medina
description: Muhammad's migration from Mecca to Medina marks the start of the Islamic calendar.

title: Conquest of Mecca
description: Muhammad and his followers peacefully took Mecca, establishing it as Islam's holiest city.

title: First Saudi State Founded
description: Muhammad ibn Saud allied with the reformer Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, founding the first Saudi state.

title: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia Unified
description: Abdulaziz ibn Saud unified the regions of the peninsula into the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

title: Discovery of Oil
description: Vast oil reserves were discovered, transforming Saudi Arabia into one of the world's wealthiest nations.

title: Vision 2030 Launched
description: Saudi Arabia announced Vision 2030, a plan to diversify its economy beyond oil.

title: Kingdom of Ebla
description: Ebla emerged as a powerful early city-state in northern Syria, known for its vast cuneiform archives.

title: Ugarit and the Alphabet
description: The city of Ugarit developed one of the earliest known alphabets, written in cuneiform script.

title: Roman Province of Syria
description: Pompey made Syria a Roman province, with Antioch becoming one of the empire's greatest cities.

title: Umayyad Caliphate in Damascus
description: The Umayyads made Damascus the capital of a vast caliphate stretching across three continents.

title: Ottoman Conquest of Syria
description: The Ottoman Empire took control of Syria, ruling the region for four centuries.

title: Independence of Syria
description: Syria gained full independence as French mandate forces withdrew from the country.

title: Syrian Civil War Begins
description: Anti-government protests escalated into a prolonged and devastating civil war.

title: Neolithic Settlement of Çatalhöyük
description: Çatalhöyük flourished in Anatolia as one of the world's earliest and largest known urban settlements.

title: Rise of the Hittite Empire
description: The Hittites built a powerful empire centered in Anatolia, rivaling Egypt and Babylon.

title: Founding of Constantinople
description: Emperor Constantine refounded Byzantium as Constantinople, the new capital of the Roman Empire.

title: Ottoman Conquest of Constantinople
description: Mehmed II captured Constantinople, ending the Byzantine Empire and establishing the Ottoman capital.

title: Reign of Suleiman the Magnificent
description: Suleiman led the Ottoman Empire to its political, military, and cultural golden age.

title: Republic of Turkey Founded
description: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk proclaimed the Republic of Turkey and became its first president.

title: Adoption of the Latin Alphabet
description: Atatürk introduced sweeping reforms, including replacing the Arabic script with a Latin-based alphabet.

title: Arrival of Islam
description: The tribes of the region that became the UAE embraced Islam during the early Islamic era.

title: Treaty with Britain
description: Coastal sheikhdoms signed a maritime truce with Britain, leading to the name Trucial States.

title: Discovery of Oil in Abu Dhabi
description: Major oil reserves were discovered in Abu Dhabi, transforming the future federation's prospects.

title: Formation of the United Arab Emirates
description: Seven emirates united to form the UAE under founding president Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan.

title: Burj Khalifa Opens
description: Dubai inaugurated the Burj Khalifa, the tallest building in the world.

title: Hope Mars Mission Launched
description: The UAE launched the Hope probe, becoming the first Arab nation to send a mission to Mars.

title: Abraham Accords Signed
description: The UAE normalized relations with Israel under the US-brokered Abraham Accords.

title: Kingdom of Saba (Sheba)
description: The Sabaean kingdom rose in Yemen, growing wealthy from the incense and spice trade.

title: Great Dam of Marib
description: The Sabaeans built the Marib Dam, an engineering marvel that irrigated a flourishing civilization.

title: Yemen Embraces Islam
description: Yemen converted to Islam during the lifetime of the Prophet Muhammad.

title: Ottoman Control of Yemen
description: The Ottoman Empire extended its rule over Yemen, contesting control with local imams.

title: North Yemen Independence
description: North Yemen gained independence from the Ottoman Empire following World War I.

title: South Yemen Independence
description: South Yemen gained independence from Britain, becoming a separate socialist state.

title: Unification of Yemen
description: North and South Yemen merged to form the unified Republic of Yemen.
